packs.title: Art, Industry and Shore
packs.promise: Explore Milwaukee through separate art, industry, history and public-space outings.

q.s: Compare a credited artwork with the building that frames it.
st: Choose one credited work in a currently open gallery or the museum's online collection.
Record one fact from its label, then identify one visible form of the museum building from a lawful public position or official image.
Sketch how the building and work create different viewing experiences; mark the artist's information separately from your interpretation.

q.s: Read two credited historical sources with their context intact.
st: Choose two sources the museum credits in an open or virtual gallery.
Record who or what each source represents, its period, and the museum's stated context without paraphrasing a person's experience as your own.
Write one careful comparison of the evidence and one question for further learning using the museum's own references.

q.s: Read architectural details while respecting an active parish.
st: Identify one building form from the public exterior, open nave or the parish's official images.
Use the free Pavilion exhibit or official walking guide to record one documented design or construction fact.
Write how the form serves both a historic building and a living congregation, keeping observation and source distinct.

packs.title: City Hall to Lakefront
packs.promise: Walk from the civic core through the Third Ward to the harbor and lakefront.

q.s: Read a historic performance venue from its lawful public approach.
st: Locate one exterior form that distinguishes the theater entrance from nearby civic or commercial buildings.
Read the operator's description of the theater's current performance role and the city's historic-district source.
Write a two-line note comparing the visible threshold with the venue's documented use.

q.s: Read former warehouse forms in today's Third Ward streets.
st: On one public block, choose two distinct warehouse-era exterior details, such as loading openings and repeated window bays.
Read the city's Third Ward plan to identify its documented industrial and warehouse character and later reuse.
Draw a block elevation that separates surviving form from current uses you can actually verify.

q.s: Compare two waterside habitats from a marked park path.
st: Choose a short open paved park segment with a lawful view of both lagoon and lake or their mapped positions.
Record one observed shoreline difference and one park-map fact; do not claim an animal sighting.
Make a two-sided habitat sketch showing how the public trail passes between the water edges.
